notes.title: Devlog #9 - Player Hosted Sessions are here!
notes.content:
Over the last month I’ve been listening to the players and one thing that was brought up was if they can host their own servers. I originally wanted to just have dedicated servers run by me, but the reality is that I can’t host servers all over the world. Well, I can. But it would break my bank account. So, with that I decided to go ahead and add the functionality for players host their own sessions. 

This means you can make a game and you`ll be the host, and your friends can connect directly to your game. This is great for regions where I don’t have dedicated servers active. The servers you can host aren’t dedicated servers, though. So, if the host closes the game or leaves, the session is destroyed, and all players are sent back to the main menu. Maybe in the future I’ll release the dedicated server tools as well. 


This took me a long time to get working. Testing locally for me is very difficult as I only have 1 working computer. Also the game logic was never really intended to cater for players that are both the server and a client at the same time. I had to go back and rework a lot of the server / client logic. Finally, it`s all working now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/14d01f45cb8143dc20f011e924f5855349b5e8ed.jpg[/img]

When you host a session, you can choose the game mode (free for all or king of the hill, more soon), whether map rotation is on / off, the map you want to play on, the rounds per map, the max players and also what weapons you want to spawn in the game! So now you can have a melee weapon only bust up, or maybe just a nade spam match. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/e1aa4879fde4f7c70b2536255e928dbd93f2e308.jpg[/img]

This whole feature release is the first part of this update. Next I`ll add an option to make sessions private, friend invites, and also add more game options like time limits, low gravity etc. 

Since the game entered early access, I`ve switched focus from the things I originally wanted to add, to the things my actual players want me to add. I`m grateful to everyone that has given me feedback and ideas so far.

-	Key remapping
-	Leaderboards 
-	Player hosted sessions
-	Single player mode against bots
-	More customization options
-	Steam cloud saves
-	Game round balancing 
-	Weapon balancing

Next update in a week!

Don`t forget to join the discord

notes.title: Leaderboards are here!
notes.content:
Hello and welcome to devlog 8. This time i`m going to talk about the new leaderboards and what`s coming next. 

Leaderboards are here!

This was something I always wanted to add to the game. I never included it into the roadmap though because I wasn’t sure of its priority compared to the other features in the pipeline. Over the last month, I realised that its important to have some form of social leaderboards. This`ll get players online a bit more, and hopefully competing against each other for the top spots!

Right now, there are 2 leaderboards. Total kills, and weekly top kills. Total kills will be a persistent statistic, showing the top 10 players ranked by multiplayer kills. Weekly kills is more like a tournament, that shows the current weeks top 10 players by kills. This will reset every 7 days, and the winner will be announced over on discord and twitter! Eventually, I want to add real prizes for these tournaments, such as [b]online store gift coupons[/b]. Let me know in the comments if you have any ideas for these prizes. 

Now I know how to quickly set up new leaderboards, I can add more based on other stats whenever needed. For example, weekly top 10 based on Free for all rounds won, or most XP gained, and so on. I can put these on a playlist to keep it varied. 

The leaderboards are done on playfab and luckily there are functions built into the playfab GSDK on unreal engine. Below shows how I can simply pull the stats based on the value name, and then get other information from the results, such as the players display name, their rank and their score. (note: you have to finish the game round in order for your stats to be uploaded to the server) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/0033bcc88412d173bf5a88d0b327815081ca385f.jpg[/img]
[i]Here i simply call the leaderboard stat "WeeklyKills" which I created on playfab. It returns information about the leaderboard itself, such as the reset time. [/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/20c9a39a250a4de9320bd951b7d8e3e63b399177.jpg[/img]
[i]Then I run a loop for the top 10 results, which are conveniently already sorted. I can get their display name, position and stat value. I also store a local set of the results and use that, instead of constantly getting data from the server every time you press the button.[/i]


Speaking of playfab, the next step is to move all the player stats and challenge unlock progress to an online cloud save. In hindsight this should`ve been done before launch, but now I fully understand how to utilize playfab online services it shouldn`t be too hard to make the switch to fully online cloud saves (don’t worry, your XP and LEVEL is already saved on the cloud).

Next up in the pipeline is localisation. I will add 2 new languages, Latam Spanish and Japanese. I`ve already set up the program side of things, now I just need to go through and localise all the content. Luckily, there aren’t too many strings to do (Beans are simple).
If you would like to see the game localised into any other languages, let me know and I`ll see what I can do. 

Jump into the discord and chat with me and the other members of the community. See you in game!

https://discord.gg/6vcRDyfVzr

notes.title: 70% Sale! Celebrating 1 month since launch
notes.content:
[h1]Bot Battle Mode is here![/h1]

Thank you to everyone who has played the game so far. The feedback I`ve received is great and people seem to enjoy the game, and that`s the most important thing for me. 

Combat Beans has been live for a month now, and since release I`ve been working through the roadmap as well as taking on board feedback from the community. So to celebrate here`s a 70% sale until Sep 26th.

One of the most common requests was to include a game mode against bots, so that people can jump on and play properly even when nobody is online. Originally, I never planned to add bots (or any major single player mode) to the game, but soon after launch I realised that there are a few hours each day where nobody is online. In those cases, it`s unfair for people who bought the game being unable to experience the game properly. So, I decided to add bots to the game, as well as a new game mode.
You can play against up to 12 bots (I find playing with more bots to be more fun) in a mode where first to get to the kill limit wins the round. Round kill limits can be selected from 10 – 100, and you can also select the difficulty of the bots as well as what weapons they will use. Check out the gameplay below!

[previewyoutube=89cXrO1xiy8;full][/previewyoutube]

As I never did AI before my technical knowledge is quite basic, but I tried to make the bots play like real players as best as I could. They jump and slide around and will melee you if you get too close, though they generally prefer to keep at range if they can. There are still times when they can be a bit derpy, but overall if you`re playing against 12 bots, there`s so much chaos all around that it`s very hard to tell. Over time, I will keep updating the AI behaviour. 

There is one problem I need to fix regarding the Bot Battle Mode, and that is the EXP gained during this mode isn’t being sent back to the playfab servers where all the player data is being stored, because that Bot Battle game mode isn’t being run on an online server on playfab. So, what I need to do is decide to have the EXP and level stored locally on your machine (a bad idea for a number of reasons) or switch to using the steam cloud storage for all the stats. Steam cloud is a much better solution for sure but will take some time for me to set up properly and debug everything. 

Another request I need to take into consideration is to add a feature so that players can host their own public / private sessions. Right now, I`m using playfabs servers to hot games dynamically, where I can easily add or remove servers whenever I need to. In the future, I think it would be great for players to host their own, so I will begin taking a look at the work required to make that happen. 

Over the coming weeks I will keep working through the original planned roadmap, like adding power-ups and team death match, As well as any bug fixing if required. 

Thank you again for playing the game! Please join the discord if you want, and be part of the growing community. 

https://discord.gg/6vcRDyfVzr

notes.title: Combat Beans is LIVE!
notes.content:
Combat Beans early access is LIVE! 

Welcome to the early access of my first game, Combat Beans! 
In this build you`ll be able to play online in 12 player servers in Free for all and King of the hill game modes. There are currently 4 multiplayer maps in the map rotation, and there are 3 rounds of gameplay in each map before it switches. More game modes like team death match are on the way, so stay tuned to the announcements.

You earn EXP in game by obliterating your enemies (or friends?), winning rounds, and capturing the zone in king of the hill. When you level up, you`ll unlock new helmet and dog tag attachments for your bean that you can proudly show off. I`ll add new cosmetic unlocks as often as I can. 
In addition, you`re able to freely customize the colors of your bean to your liking, so go wild and show off your style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/5f06c68d41a2d3749799de6a882df76de85831b2.jpg[/img]

I also added a single player mode, the time trial challenges. Each challenge requires you to complete the objective within the time limit, and there are 3 times you can get. Bronze, Silver and Gold. Right now, there are 8 challenges, and they require you to get from A to B within the time limit. Soon I’ll be adding more challenges as well as different types of objectives, such as pulling off trick shots, hitting all the targets in a map before the time runs out, and more. 


I plan to run the game in early access for 3 – 6 months. During that time, I’ll be doing any bug fixes, whilst working through the roadmap (which you can see in game by clicking the “roadmap” button in the main menu). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/4491e2e10c51a99ccf97c2b91c02207d3fc13d82.jpg[/img]

I want to thank everyone for taking part in the early access and for all the feedback you can give me. This is my first game and I want to make sure It`s as fun as possible for everyone, so if you have any ideas, questions, or feedback, or just want to be part of the community and have a chat, please join the discord or leave a comment below. 
Thank you all once again and see you in game!

Now most of the major issues and features for the upcoming early access launch are finished, I was finally able to spend some time adding all the cosmetic unlocks. 

You will be able to unlock new helmet attachments that plop directly onto your standard issue helmet, and also new dog tags and neck attachments to swap out your regular dog tag with.

notes.title: Devlog #6 - Chat, 4.27 update and bug fixes
notes.content:
[b]Devlog #6[/b]

I`ve been busy over the last couple of months working on the game and getting it ready for release. As a public release gets closer, I need to make sure all of the major bugs are fixed and tested. Some of the major bugs and improvements I`ve made are listed below.

[b]•	Update to unreal engine 4.27 [/b]– This is a stop gap before doing a full update to 5.x. Unfortunately, there were a lot of engine errors going straight to 5, so for now I decided to get it updated to 4.27, whilst working on other features for the game. I hope to be able to get the game updated to UE 5 as soon as possible, but I don’t want to risk breaking a ton of other things in the game in the process. As of now the 4.27 build works perfectly fine.

[b]•	Fixes to projectiles,[/b] client and server side – this was a persistent issue in the game from the start. The original system was somewhat simple in its implementation. Arguably too simple. I have now created client side and server side projectiles, which means that the overall feeling of the gunplay is much smoother for clients, regardless of your latency in game. There was also a long running bug where some projectiles wouldn’t multicast their impact hits to all connected clients (which was driving me insane), but this has finally been fixed in the new system.


[b]•	Network improvements[/b] – this isn’t really specific to any one change in the code, but over the last month I`ve been spending a lot of my time identifying where I can reduce network data usage during gameplay. This is important for me as I will be paying for all hosted servers out of my own pocket, so I want the servers to be as optimized as possible. This also will result in better network performance for all players. One of the specific things I`ve been doing is using RepNotify bool variables to trigger events on all clients instead of multicast RPCs. This reduces data usage (for those events) by approximately 80%. 

[b]•	Multiplayer text chat –[/b] a simple thing but required. Players can insult each other’s bean status in-game. Chat can be turned off from the control options sub menu. 

[b]•	Cosmetic asset optimization[/b] – all cosmetics now use soft object references in the game code. That means that the player character wont need load all the assets into memory by default, and will only load the required asset as and when its required. This sounds like a no brainer (and it is, to be fair) but it required a re-work of quite a bit of the logic to make sure the game can handle loading and unloading the assets. The big trade off with soft object references is that you need to manually load and unload those assets from memory, and that can be a pain to get right. 

[b]•	Gameplay balance! [/b]– finally i`ve been able to start doing gameplay tests. Immediately after the test I wrote down a list of things to change and tweak according to the feedback of the testers. One of which is quite apparent in the gameplay video below, and that is the speed of the projectiles. All bullets in the game are actual physical projectiles flying through space, unlike hit scan weapons (like bullets in CS). After thorough play testing, I can safely say the bullet speed right now across the board can be about 2x faster. Also I`ve raised the damage levels of all bullets by about 25 – 30%. This will make gunplay with fast firing machine guns a little more lethal. As of now, explosive weapons like the bazooka, grenade launcher and grenades are definitely the most effective weapons. 

[b]•	“The slime gun is too strong”[/b] – this was funny in the last play test. I dunno, I kind of like having a gun that basically roots you to the ground and stops you from dashing. You know when your screen gets green, you`ll start to scream…

You can see some of the last play test in the video below! 

[previewyoutube=zjltEaOvE5I;full][/previewyoutube]

Leave a comment and let me know what you think of the game play so far. 


In the next update, i`ll be continuing on bug fixes and optimization, reworking some UI elements such as the health bar, and adding a hit scan weapon as a test to see how it plays. I will also begin work on the 4th and 5th maps, and add a few more helmet and dog tag unlocks! Still a lot of work to do, but things are moving forward faster than ever. 
After that, stat tracking is next on the menu.

Come join the discord!

notes.title: Good News!
notes.content:
Firstly..
Bust out the tiny violins for a sad, short song. 

Over the last couple of months, I’ve been dealing with a new illness that unfortunately manifested itself out of nowhere and has, basically, fucked me up. Thankfully I’m dealing with it a bit better now and can plan my time a lot better. Hopefully this Friday ill know exactly what the problem is, but for the time being I’m able to spend more time on this game, which means you can put those tiny violins away, damnit! 

[b]Dash Ability[/b]

I originally wanted the movement mechanics to be quite simple, aiming to avoid it turning into a movement-shooter, like gunz or S4-League (although those games were great). That said, the beans needed[i] something [/i]to spice up the movement of the game. I knew I didn’t want to add a traditional sprint / stamina bar, so a short, directional dash ability fills the gap quite nicely. 
To do it, press shift + wasd and you`ll quickly dash a short distance in that direction. You have full directional control during the dash as well, which means you can dash around corners. 
Dashing into players will also knock them back a considerable distance (depending on the angle you hit them at). This can be used to hurl them into a fire trap or into the sea. You can knock back multiple players too if they’re all bunched up together. 
You can still shoot and melee someone whilst dashing too. And all the knockback force stacks, so dashing into someone then blicky them with the shotty will send them flying miles.  
 
New Weapons!
[b]Slime gun[/b]
The original slime gun (originally the glob gun) was really a placeholder weapon of sorts. I want guns to be unique and not just bullets-with-different-stats. So, the slime gun now fires balls of green slime, that cause a slowing effect if they impact you. The effect doesn’t last long, but during that time your ground movement speed will be reduced. The gun itself also does reasonable damage, though its got a shorter range and now fires 1 larger projectile instead of multiple smaller ones. Im still playing with the balance, like fire rate, accuracy, etc.

[b]Grenade launcher[/b]
This fires grenades in an arc that cause a lot of damage in an area on impact. Uses less ammo per shot than the bazooka (3 instead of 5) but care needs to be taken when firing at beans close to you. 

Ill get footage of these new weapons and the dash in the next big play test I have lined up. stay tuned.


[b]
Optimizations[/b]
This is an ongoing task but over the last few months i`ve made a few key changes to how asset loading is handled in the background. This simply means things aren`t permanently loaded all the time which results in some better performance. Besides this ive made a ton of subtle improvements to material shaders and textures in order to keep performance relatively good across most machines.

[b]Update to Unreal Engine 5[/b]
This unfortunately hasn’t been completed [b]yet.[/b] Right now, the game is fine on 4.26 however there are some key features of 5 that I want to use. I get approximately 1 billion engine errors when trying to update the project to 5 and I can`t figure out exactly what`s causing it. I`ll keep everyone posted about this.
 
[b]Release plans [/b]
I want the game to launch with as many features as I can add as possible. Some key remaining features that are yet to be added include in game chat, team death match, a single player component to the game (at the very least a tutorial level) and a challenge mode with specific unlocks. There`s still a lot of front end UX stuff that needs to be done. 
As of now there are 3 maps, 10 weapons and 2 game modes. Also a functional level system, cosmetic unlocks (about 50 or so for now) and character customization. 
I will add extra maps, guns and cosmetics during the early access period, and I’ve already got the next map/weapon/cosmetic theme pack planned.

Next devlog will be next Friday. 
Don’t forget the join the discord. All are welcome. 


Thanks again for following the project

notes.title: Devlog #4 for Combat Beans! - Custom Beans and Unlocks
notes.content:
[h1]Unlocks[/h1]

Welcome to Devlog #4

This week’s topic is showcasing a handful of unlocks.

You gain XP in combat beans by doing all sorts of things. Participating in game rounds, killing players and of course winning rounds. Every time you level up, you`ll unlock some new items to slap on to your bean. 

Currently, these are split into 2 groups. Helmet attachments and the dog tags / neck attachments. 

The helmet attachments fit on top (or somewhere) on the helmet of your bean. They don’t replace the helmet entirely. You still have the ability to change the colours of the helmet underneath the attachment however you like, and combined with a ton of different attachments , you can make some really unique combinations. 

The dog tags are similar, and offer a ton of different colours and visual effects like animated neon glows and funky scanlines. There are also completely custom meshes that replace the dog tags entirely, like the ammo bandoleers, medals (awarded for bravery, of course) and a ton more. 

Along with custom colours , you can mix and match the unlocks to make some unique combos that no other bean would have. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/293920dbddb75bab596566df2e56e7e8ed9a4378.jpg[/img]


So far, everyone thinks the night vision goggles are best (RIP radar ☹ )

[h3]Custom unlocks for participating in community events[/h3]

You want something that LITERALLY no other player would ever have? Well I hope so, because a soon-to-be added feature will allow me to award individual steam IDs with 100% unique unlocks that nobody else would be able to equip, ever. These will be linked to community events, such as art events or best gameplay video. Be sure to hop into the discord to keep up to date with all that jazz. 

The game will launch with plenty to unlock, and more will be added all the time, especially during events. 
Stay tuned for devlog #5!

notes.title: Devlog #3 for Combat Beans! - Maps and UI
notes.content:
[h1]New Maps[/h1]

2 new maps have been added. Both of these have some indoor areas, as well as a variety of floating platforms to get around to some hard-to-reach areas. Here are some screenshots.

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_fbdaa929b4f54fc6ada13e57f121bb60~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_a011b994b3d648dcb47ae5c8c25845f1~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_76e23cc1844f4ce4868678725cc5199d~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_d98dba0fb4dc4299970f4a4dd3875986~mv2.jpg[/img]

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_4488300cb76e428fa47b46fd10258ca6~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_c544ba63783d439184a8057f9702c21e~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_b4a470c7916a460fa2e1bdb343d5fcb7~mv2.jpg[/img]
[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_4a0be496945b43ad9b19f2f8102797f6~mv2.jpg[/img]


The hardest part of making the maps is the original blocking out of the major shapes and landmarks. It can be easy to spend too much time focusing on one tiny area, only to realize it just doesn’t work out when combined with the rest of the level. A lot of time gets wasted that way, so I split it down into 4 main steps. 

1)	create blocking areas, figuring out where players will be able to run around. 
2)	create line of sight blocking terrain
3)	detailing of landscape height
4)	foliage, props, decals and all other small details.  

Never start with foliage! I wasted too much time re-doing it over and over again. This was because I would make adjustments to the landscape over time, and that caused a lot of foliage to be in the wrong place. procedural foliage can be set up, but the maps here aren’t really ginormous so procedural generation doesn’t particularly save me much time either compared to manually doing it at the end. so always wait until everything else is done first before adding foliage. 

[h1]New ammo counter UI
[/h1]

[b]Old and busted[/b]

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_077857cce7f8422fa62e8e2a5add6abc~mv2.jpg[/img]

[b]New hotness[/b]

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/627955_1ecf1f33406b4120b9693096b11f2425~mv2.jpg[/img]


The new UI now displays an icon showing the weapon that`s equipped, and also the ammo cost per shot. this is important as all guns have different ammo costs when firing, and as I add more guns it`ll be too hard to remember all the costs off by heart. 
Also, the main ammo counter will change to dark grey when you have less ammo than the current cost per shot. this lets you know that even though you have some ammo, you might not have enough to fire the current weapon. 

I`m thinking of switching to a video format for these devlogs from next week. I`ll have to see how much time it takes me and also which format people prefer.

notes.title: Devlog #2 for Combat Beans! - Guns
notes.content:
[h1][b]Welcome to devlog #2! [/b][/h1]
We need guns, lots of guns. 
Well, we have a handful for now. Here they are. But first heres a bit of a description of the gunplay in the game.

As you can tell from the gameplay trailer, there are no hitscan weapons in the game. every single bullet is a real projectile in 3D space. Each weapon type has its own variables, such as speed of the bullets, damage, knockback force, cool down between shots, ammo cost and so on. Weapons are balanced by their “ammo cost per shot”, as all weapon types in the game use the same type of ammo. This means you can have 100 ammo and fire off 100 shots with the shotgun, or 20 shots with the bazooka. Each gun works best in different situations, like some work great at long range whereas others are perfect for tight encounters with multiple enemies. 

[b]The assault rifle[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/7b089ca58b46df3c9c9b3dd78a5d56f94e62acde.jpg[/img]

My personal favourite. It has a moderate rate of fire, decent damage and range and standard ammo consumption. It’s the mainstay of any Bean militia. It is most commonly found in the Grasslands map but still pops up in other places too. 

[b]Shotgun[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/35f13430fc5fa04ff4ae7ebb25dab4478a31b72a.jpg[/img]

My personal favourite. I call it the potty-shotty, because fools crap themselves when Great for short range combat, you can blast some poor unfortunate fool into the ocean if you angle your shot right. Fires a spread of pellets that each do low damage, but at close range it can be lethal. Slow rate of fire but at close range it has the best ratio of ammo-per-bean kill power in the game. 

[b]Minigun[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/5d36d44957de77f44642eae6948ee4ae1c8cece2.jpg[/img]

This blaps out a ton of lead at a high rate of fire over a moderate range. Can burn through a ton of ammo quickly, and each bullet is relatively low damage. The sheer rate of fire however means you can suppress most enemy beans in front of you, and multiple hits in a row can knockback players pretty far. Very inaccurate however (a standard bean struggles to lift a gun the same size as them)

[b]Autocannon[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/3fc62a665a87e64367bae124cd0df9adec0cb8a2.jpg[/img]

A high-powered portable cannon that fires shells over a long range. Difficult to use due to the shells needing time to hit the target, so practice is required. It deals high damage though, and can bust up some beans in a few shots. Has a moderate rate of fire and reasonable accuracy, but will gobble up ammo much faster than the rifle, if you aren’t careful. 

[b]Dual Uzis [/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/77a1cdc3d207eb94d36d9a61fd99653624b50bb9.jpg[/img]

Great over short range, the uzis unleash a ton of lead in a general area extremely fast. Low damage but high rate of fire makes it good for people who have collected enough ammo to spray and pray (to the Bean Gods upstairs, or downstairs, they haven’t figured it out yet). Many shots that hit the target can end up knocking beans into traps or the ocean. 

[b]Glob gun[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/ca67f5d2542ea62094d5bb9e234c26540f2714fe.jpg[/img]

A strange weapon indeed. Something between a shotgun and a pistol. It fires a spread of toxic bullets at a short range but at a much faster rate than the shotgun. Like an auto-shotty. Lower damage but good knockback ability and moderate consumption of ammo makes this an interesting choice for close range combat.

[b]Bazooka[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/d3faebd40c1779cbdd20e822d595eab350db3f75.jpg[/img]

A classic. A tube that fires a rocket over a very long distance. High ammo cost per shot but the explosion damages anyone near it (even yourself) and has a high knockback. If you have enough health you can use it to get around the map. 

[b]Grenades[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43126175/169e96bdd2d9ecd4c1e795a2cbd8e9929fd2c0f5.jpg[/img]

A throwable explosive. Explosion causes a large aoe and high damage, though harder to use when under pressure. Holding left click will cook the grenade, showing you the throwing arc. Or just spam it with left click as I do. Screw it. 

Let me know what you think. Ideas for new guns? Join the discord and share you ideas with everyone!

notes.title: Devlog #1 for Combat Beans!
notes.content:
Welcome to Devlog #1 for Combat Beans: Total Mayhem! Over the next few months I`m going to be doing weekly devlogs to show you all what the current state of the game is, and also any interesting bits and pieces that are being worked on at the moment. This week, You`ll see the list of features of in the game as of its current latest build, and also some of the concept art. 

[b]Current state of the game[/b]
First up, the following features have been fully implemented and after internal testing, everything is working as intended* 

•	[b]Bean colour customisation [/b]– You can freely change the body part colours of your bean.
•	[b]Level progression and experience system[/b] – You will get EXP for participating in game rounds, killing other players, winning rounds and so on. As you get more exp and level up you`ll unlock cool new cosmetics like dog tags and helmet attachments (this part will be finished soon)
•	[b]Gameplay mechanics[/b] – movement, gunplay, game round loops are all working fine. This is something that will always be looked at according to feedback, and new gameplay mechanics will be added during the early access period. 
•	[b]Free for All[/b] and [b]King of the Hill[/b] game modes – 2 working game modes, both are FFA but there will be team variants of these too.
•	[b]Dynamically scaling servers[/b] – This is mostly back end related, but the servers are all spun up dynamically based on the server load. This is handy as it means there wont be a ton of servers running with few players online. 
•	[b]Regional servers[/b] – EU and East US for now, with West US and at least 1 Asia server coming soon (according to demand)
•	[b]2 maps[/b] – these will be showcased in more detail in a later devlog, but currently we have 2 maps completed and 1 more in the concept stage. 
•	[b]Steam achievements[/b] – currently there are 19, I plan to have 25 for launch.
[b]
Concept art vs final in-game assets[/b]
Here is some of the concept art for terrain and level props, and also how they look in the game. I wanted something simple and clean, with lots of modular capability. All the model materials are using vertex colour channels, which lets me easily change the colours of the parts to whatever I want without needing new albedo textures.
